summary: Constructs a canonical actual USC upper relaxation from all affinoid Shilov limits and proves the exact nonnegative defect K=D(mu)-D(nu). Positivity and original existence remain unresolved.
detailedSummary: The upper relaxed tail limit is normalized, common to maximizing nets and determined by all finite affinoid Shilov boundaries. It agrees with the uniform Gauss limit but may exceed the full-point tuple. One-sided variations give K>=0 and integral w(nu-mu)<=K. A precise, unproved two-sided perturbation condition would force nu=mu; neither this condition nor finite-energy analytic membership is established.
text:
This uses earlier own notes n1 and n2; the local uniform sector n3 is relevant only to the stated unresolved geometric step. The conclusions are a canonical actual USC UPPER RELAXATION and an exact dual defect, not an analytic finite-energy solution.

Let a_i be a normalized net maximizing the full bounded dual for positive mass-two finite-dual mu. With n2 limits e=lim Ea_i, p=lim integral a_i MA(a_i), r=lim integral a_i mu=e-B, and nu=weak-lim MA(a_i), define
K=p-r=B-D(nu)=lim_i integral a_i(MA(a_i)-mu).
All equalities follow from n2's exact D(nu)=e-p. The sign and the entire allowable first-variation conclusion can be proved explicitly. Write k_i=integral a_i(MA(a_i)-mu). For0<t<=1, the second derivative of Fmu((1-t)a_i) has absolute value<=12C, because Q_theta_s a_i(a_i)<=6C. Integral Taylor remainder gives Fmu((1-t)a_i)>=Fmu(a_i)-t k_i-6Ct^2. Its value is at most B, so k_i>=-epsilon_i/t-6Ct. First take the net limit, then t->0, proving K>=0.
For fixed normalized w, D=max(C,-Ew,0), the Hilbert inequality Q_T(w-a_i)<=2Q_T(w)+2Q_T(a_i) and n1's moment bounds give a second derivative bound48D along (1-t)a_i+tw. Therefore
integral w(MA(a_i)-mu)-k_i<=epsilon_i/t+24Dt.
Taking the two limits gives integral w(nu-mu)<=K for EVERY w in C. Constants remove the normalization. These one-sided inequalities on a convex positivity class do not imply nu=mu: C is not closed under negation or arbitrary positive scaling, although its linear span is dense.

For clarity, a sufficient replacement variation condition has a complete implication proof. Suppose a uniformly dense real test space W admits for every h some t_h>0,L_h<infinity such that late actual weights a_i+th belong to C for |t|<=t_h and
|Fmu(a_i+th)-Fmu(a_i)-t integral h(MA(a_i)-mu)|<=L_h t^2.
Both signs and maximality imply |integral h(MA(a_i)-mu)|<=epsilon_i/t+L_h t. Passing first to the weak net limit and then t->0 yields integral h(nu-mu)=0. Density and finite masses give nu=mu. The needed actual perturbations are NOT proved; theta degenerates off its coordinate skeleton. This implication also supplies no analytic representative by itself.

Canonical actual USC reconstruction. Let ell(x)=lim_i a_i(x) at every full point, supplied by n2. For each tail i set b_i(y)=sup_{j>=i}a_j(y), and R_i(x)=inf_{ordinary O containing x} sup_{y in O}b_i(y). If R_i(x)<c for a finite c, one such O gives the same strict upper bound at all its points, so R_i is USC, including -infinity. The R_i decrease, hence R=inf_i R_i is USC with R<=0. This is a topological construction; none of b_i,R_i,R is thereby psh or generated. Adding a continuous local rho commutes with upper relaxation and its decreasing infimum.

There is a precise all-Shilov formula, independent of the maximizing net:
rho(x)+R(x)=inf_{affinoid neighborhoods A of x in the chart} max_{xi in Gamma_A}(rho(xi)+ell(xi)).
Proof: every such pure surface affinoid has a FINITE Shilov boundary of full graded dimension two by GR6.3. Each q_j=rho+a_j is classically psh, so GR6.4 bounds q_j on A by max_Gamma_A q_j. This finite maximum converges to max_Gamma_A(rho+ell), and x is in the ordinary interior of A. Hence the upper relaxed limit is at most that maximum and then its infimum. Conversely for any ordinary neighborhood O and any tail i, choose an affinoid neighborhood A contained in O, using goodness and boundarylessness. Its finite Shilov points lie in O; their tail suprema are at least their finite limits. Thus sup_{y in O,j>=i}q_j(y)>=max_Gamma_A(rho+ell)>=the stated affinoid infimum. Infimize over O and i to prove the reverse inequality. The formula glues across continuous affine reference changes. Since ell is common to all maximizing nets, so is R.

Pointwise tail suprema give ell(x)<=R(x) at full points. On the real Gauss torus the restrictions g_i are equi-Lipschitz and pointwise Cauchy, hence uniformly Cauchy by a finite grid argument. Their continuous uniform limit g has maximum zero. Since a_i(y)<=g_i(tau(y)), upper relaxation gives R(y)<=g(tau(y)). At Gauss points R>=ell=g, so R|S=g and max_XR=0. In particular R is an actual nontrivial USC function, with possible poles.

This does NOT establish agreement R=ell at every full point, classical psh positivity, membership in an adequate actual finite-energy domain, energy E(R)=e, identification nu=MA(R), or nu=mu. GR6.5 assumes full POINTWISE convergence to an already USC function; the present full-point tuple plus upper relaxation does not meet that hypothesis. Decreasing-net closure cannot be applied to unproved positive tail suprema or their regularizations. Note n3 supplies uniform convergence only on the specified compact finite-Gauss-fibre family, not the missing Shilov-neighborhood basis. The original arbitrary-support existence and representability gates remain intact. Entire proofs appear in scoped-paper.tex and the separate whole proof-companion.txt.
